title: TOEFL iBT Reading Practice Test 20
instructions: Read each passage carefully and answer all questions. You have 35 minutes. Questions test factual understanding, vocabulary, inference, and the ability to identify main ideas.

passages.title: Climate Change and Polar Ice
passages.text:
The Arctic and Antarctic regions contain some of Earth's most sensitive indicators of climate change. Polar ice sheets and sea ice reflect approximately 80 to 90 percent of incoming solar radiation back to space, a property known as albedo. When ice melts, darker ocean water is exposed, which absorbs significantly more solar radiation, causing further warming in a self-reinforcing cycle termed the ice-albedo feedback. This mechanism makes polar regions exceptionally responsive to even modest increases in global temperature, amplifying climate change effects worldwide.

Observations from satellite records beginning in the late 1970s have documented dramatic changes in polar ice extent. Arctic sea ice has declined by approximately 13 percent per decade since 1979, with the most severe losses occurring during summer months when ice coverage reaches its annual minimum. The Arctic experienced particularly rapid warming between 2000 and 2020, a phenomenon scientists call Arctic amplification. Several factors contribute to this accelerated warming: as sea ice declines, the ice-albedo feedback intensifies; warm Atlantic water masses advect northward into the Arctic Ocean; and atmospheric moisture increases as warming allows the air to hold more water vapour.

Greenland's ice sheet, which covers an area roughly the size of Mexico and contains enough water to raise global sea levels by approximately 7 metres if fully melted, is losing mass at an accelerating rate. Early records from the 1990s indicated net annual ice loss of roughly 50 billion tonnes per year, but by the 2010s this rate had increased to approximately 280 billion tonnes per year. Summer surface melting now extends far into the interior of the ice sheet where in the past only the margins experienced thawing. This expansion of the melting zone indicates that temperatures at Greenland have risen substantially and persistently above historical norms.

The Antarctic ice sheet presents a more complex pattern. While the continent's interior is slowly accumulating snow, the ice shelves surrounding Antarctica — massive floating extensions of the ice sheet — have experienced catastrophic collapse. The Larsen B ice shelf disintegrated almost entirely between 1998 and 2002, an event that shocked glaciologists given the shelf's apparent stability over previous millennia. Ice shelf collapse removes a natural dam that restrains the flow of inland glaciers, causing them to accelerate toward the ocean. In some regions, glacier velocity has doubled or tripled following shelf collapse, dramatically increasing the rate at which ice enters the ocean and thus raising sea levels.

The consequences of polar ice loss extend far beyond sea level rise. Reduced sea ice and ice sheet melt diminish habitat for species dependent on ice, including polar bears, walruses, and ice seals. Indigenous peoples of the Arctic, particularly the Inuit, face existential threats as traditional hunting grounds disappear and infrastructure built on permafrost becomes unstable. Disruption of regional ocean currents and atmospheric circulation patterns could have global climate implications. The melting of vast quantities of fresh water into the ocean alters regional salinity and ocean density structures that drive major currents such as the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation. Understanding and projecting the trajectory of polar ice loss remains one of the most critical challenges in climate science.

passages.title: Watson and Crick: DNA Discovery
passages.text:
The elucidation of DNA's three-dimensional structure in 1953 ranks among the most pivotal scientific achievements of the twentieth century. James Watson and Francis Crick, working at Cambridge University with critical contributions from experimental data provided by Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins at King's College London, proposed the double helix model of deoxyribonucleic acid. This achievement was not the work of isolated individuals but rather emerged from the integration of findings across multiple disciplines: X-ray crystallography, organic chemistry, physics, and molecular biology.

Rosalind Franklin's X-ray crystallography was essential to determining DNA's physical structure. Using a technique called X-ray diffraction, Franklin directed X-rays at crystalline DNA samples and photographed the resulting diffraction patterns. Her legendary Photograph 51, taken in 1952, provided the clearest evidence that DNA adopted a helical form. The regular, repeating patterns in the diffraction images revealed that DNA possessed a regular, repeating structure with helical symmetry. Franklin's meticulous experimental work also quantified key parameters: the distance between helical turns, the spacing of atoms within the molecule, and the diameter of the helix. Without these precise measurements, the correct model could not have been proposed.

Watson and Crick employed model-building approaches that integrated Franklin's crystallographic data with chemical knowledge about nucleotides — the molecular subunits comprising DNA. They constructed physical models from metal plates and wire, testing different configurations to identify which would satisfy both the chemical constraints and the structural parameters derived from Franklin's data. The double helix model elegantly explained how DNA could carry genetic information: the two strands are complementary, with adenine (A) always pairing with thymine (T) and guanine (G) with cytosine (C). This complementary base-pairing provided an immediate logical mechanism for DNA replication and heredity. The model also suggested how mutations might arise through errors in base pairing.

The discovery's significance lay not merely in explaining DNA's structure but in illuminating the molecular basis of heredity. Before 1953, while scientists understood that DNA carried genetic information, the physical mechanism by which this information was stored and transmitted remained opaque. The double helix model provided that mechanism: genetic information is encoded in the sequence of base pairs along the DNA strand, and during replication, each strand serves as a template for synthesising a complementary strand. This insight unified molecular biology and transformed biological science by revealing that life's diversity and continuity rest upon chemical principles.

The attribution of credit for the DNA structure discovery has remained historically contentious. While Watson and Crick received the 1962 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, Rosalind Franklin had died in 1958 and was therefore ineligible under Nobel rules at that time (the prize is not awarded posthumously). Franklin's experimental contributions were indispensable, yet she was not formally acknowledged in the award. Contemporary assessments increasingly recognise Franklin's central role in the discovery and debate whether the historical narrative has adequately credited her contributions relative to those of her male colleagues. This episode illustrates broader patterns in the history of science where women's contributions have sometimes been obscured or marginalised in narratives of major discoveries.

questions.prompt: According to paragraph 1, what percentage of solar radiation is reflected by polar ice?
questions.correctAnswer: Approximately 80 to 90 percent
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1 states that polar ice 'reflect approximately 80 to 90 percent of incoming solar radiation back to space.'
options: Approximately 20 to 30 percent
Approximately 50 to 60 percent
Approximately 80 to 90 percent
Nearly 100 percent

questions.prompt: The word 'albedo' in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to:
questions.correctAnswer: the reflectivity of a surface
questions.explanation: 'Albedo' is a scientific term describing the proportion of light that a surface reflects, particularly in the context of solar radiation.
options: the ability to absorb heat
the reflectivity of a surface
the temperature of ice
the density of glaciers

questions.prompt: According to paragraph 2, at what rate has Arctic sea ice declined since 1979?
questions.correctAnswer: Approximately 13 percent per decade
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 states that 'Arctic sea ice has declined by approximately 13 percent per decade since 1979.'
options: Approximately 5 percent per decade
Approximately 13 percent per decade
Approximately 25 percent per decade
Approximately 50 percent per decade

questions.prompt: What can be inferred from paragraph 2 about Arctic amplification?
questions.correctAnswer: Multiple mechanisms combine to cause unusually rapid warming in the Arctic
questions.explanation: The passage explains that Arctic amplification is caused by 'several factors' including ice-albedo feedback, ocean water advection, and increased atmospheric moisture, suggesting multiple reinforcing mechanisms.
options: Arctic warming is caused by a single dominant factor
Arctic warming has stopped in recent years
Multiple mechanisms combine to cause unusually rapid warming in the Arctic
Arctic amplification is unrelated to sea ice changes

questions.prompt: Why does the author mention that Greenland's ice sheet contains enough water to raise sea levels by approximately 7 metres in paragraph 3?
questions.correctAnswer: To illustrate the potentially catastrophic consequences of ice sheet melting
questions.explanation: This detail emphasises the magnitude of risk posed by Greenland's ice loss, suggesting severe global consequences.
options: To show that Greenland's ice sheet is not melting
To illustrate the potentially catastrophic consequences of ice sheet melting
To argue that sea levels have already risen 7 metres
To explain why glaciologists were surprised by changes

questions.prompt: According to paragraph 3, which of the following is NOT mentioned regarding Greenland's ice loss?
questions.correctAnswer: The ice sheet's total disappearance within the next decade
questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 discusses rate increases and expansion of the melting zone, but does not claim the ice sheet will disappear within a decade.
options: Rate of ice loss accelerated from the 1990s to the 2010s
Melting now extends into the interior of the ice sheet
The ice sheet's total disappearance within the next decade
Net annual ice loss has increased significantly

questions.prompt: According to paragraph 4, what was the consequence of the Larsen B ice shelf collapse?
questions.correctAnswer: Inland glaciers accelerated toward the ocean, increasing sea level rise
questions.explanation: Paragraph 4 states that ice shelf collapse 'removes a natural dam that restrains the flow of inland glaciers, causing them to accelerate toward the ocean,' thus increasing ice discharge and sea levels.
options: The Antarctic interior began to melt rapidly
Inland glaciers accelerated toward the ocean, increasing sea level rise
Ocean temperatures decreased significantly
Sea ice in the Arctic expanded

questions.prompt: The word 'catastrophic' in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to:
questions.correctAnswer: sudden and devastating
questions.explanation: 'Catastrophic' describes something that causes sudden, severe, and wide-ranging negative effects.
options: gradual and expected
sudden and devastating
temporary and reversible
minor and insignificant

questions.prompt: Which best expresses the essential information in this sentence: 'The melting of vast quantities of fresh water into the ocean alters regional salinity and ocean density structures that drive major currents such as the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation.'
questions.correctAnswer: Melting ice freshens the ocean and disrupts the water density differences that drive major ocean currents
questions.explanation: The sentence explains that freshwater input changes salinity and density, which affects ocean circulation.
options: Ocean currents cause ice to melt at an accelerated rate
Melting ice freshens the ocean and disrupts the water density differences that drive major ocean currents
The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation is strengthened by ice melt
Fresh water has no effect on ocean salinity

questions.prompt: Complete a summary of the passage. Select THREE answer choices that express the most important ideas.
questions.correctAnswer: A,C,E
questions.explanation: The passage's main themes are polar ice's reflectivity and the ice-albedo feedback (A), documented dramatic ice loss at both poles (C), and broad environmental and social consequences (E).
options: A. Polar ice reflects most solar radiation, and ice loss triggers the ice-albedo feedback that accelerates warming.
B. Arctic sea ice loss is caused entirely by increasing atmospheric carbon dioxide.
C. Both Arctic sea ice and major ice sheets (Greenland and Antarctic ice shelves) are experiencing rapid, accelerating loss.
D. Polar ice loss has no effect on sea levels or ocean currents.
E. Ice loss threatens species, indigenous peoples, and global ocean circulation patterns.
F. Antarctica's interior is warming faster than Greenland's ice sheet.

clear explanation or clarification
discovery or invention
publication or dissemination

questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 states that Photograph 51 'provided the clearest evidence that DNA adopted a helical form.'

That DNA adopted a helical form
That DNA could replicate itself
That DNA carried genetic information

questions.prompt: Why does the author explain the complementary base-pairing rule (A with T, G with C) in paragraph 3?

questions.explanation: The base-pairing rule is presented as a key insight that the double helix model provided, explaining how DNA could store and transmit genetic information.
options: To prove that Rosalind Franklin's data was incorrect
To show how the double helix model explained the mechanism of genetic information storage and replication
To argue that mutations never occur in DNA
To demonstrate that Watson and Crick invented the genetic code

questions.prompt: What can be inferred from paragraph 4 about the significance of the double helix model?
questions.correctAnswer: It unified molecular biology by revealing the chemical basis of heredity
questions.explanation: Paragraph 4 states the model 'unified molecular biology' and 'transformed biological science by revealing that life's diversity and continuity rest upon chemical principles.'
options: It was important only for theoretical understanding
It unified molecular biology by revealing the chemical basis of heredity
It explained why mutations never occur
It proved that genetics and chemistry were unrelated

questions.prompt: According to paragraph 5, which of the following is NOT mentioned regarding the attribution of credit for the DNA discovery?
questions.correctAnswer: Rosalind Franklin shared the Nobel Prize with Watson and Crick
questions.explanation: Paragraph 5 explicitly states Franklin was ineligible for the Nobel Prize because she had died and the prize is not awarded posthumously.
options: Watson and Crick received the 1962 Nobel Prize
Rosalind Franklin had died before the Nobel Prize was awarded
Rosalind Franklin shared the Nobel Prize with Watson and Crick
Franklin's contributions have been historically marginalised

questions.prompt: According to paragraph 2, what specific measurements did Franklin's X-ray diffraction provide?
questions.correctAnswer: The distance between helical turns, atom spacing, and helix diameter
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 states Franklin 'quantified key parameters: the distance between helical turns, the spacing of atoms within the molecule, and the diameter of the helix.'
options: The chemical composition of nucleotides
The sequence of base pairs
The distance between helical turns, atom spacing, and helix diameter
The rate of DNA replication

questions.prompt: The word 'marginalised' in paragraph 5 is closest in meaning to:
questions.correctAnswer: treated as unimportant or secondary
questions.explanation: 'Marginalised' means pushed to the edges or treated as less important than deserved.
options: physically separated
treated as unimportant or secondary
given excessive credit
excluded entirely

questions.prompt: Which best expresses the essential information in this sentence: 'The double helix model provided that mechanism: genetic information is encoded in the sequence of base pairs along the DNA strand, and during replication, each strand serves as a template for synthesising a complementary strand.'
questions.correctAnswer: The double helix model explained how genetic information is stored in base pair sequences and copied during replication
questions.explanation: The sentence explains the mechanism by which DNA stores and reproduces genetic information.
options: Genetic information is stored only in the order of nucleotides
The double helix model explained how genetic information is stored in base pair sequences and copied during replication
Base pairs are less important than the helical structure
Replication involves synthesizing entirely new DNA rather than using templates

questions.prompt: Select THREE answer choices that express the most important ideas in the passage.
questions.correctAnswer: A,C,F
questions.explanation: The passage emphasises the integrated nature of the discovery (A), the complementary base-pairing model explaining heredity (C), and historical credit attribution issues (F).
options: A. DNA's double helix structure was discovered through integrated contributions from X-ray crystallography, chemistry, and model-building approaches.
B. Watson and Crick performed all of the experimental work on DNA crystallography.
C. The double helix model revealed that genetic information is encoded in base pair sequences and explained how DNA replicates.
D. Rosalind Franklin's contributions were completely unknown until after the Nobel Prize was awarded.
E. The discovery of DNA's structure was the work of isolated individuals rather than collaborative effort.
F. The historical narrative of DNA's discovery has not fully credited Rosalind Franklin's indispensable contributions.
